pr.title: Rebuild an installer venv whose Python is gone
pr.head: f55427b6564f2aa51be8f2616d1476f5ab597022

summary: install.sh installs Projector's project command. When pipx is on the machine it uses pipx. Without it, the installer makes a Python virtual environment (a venv) of its own, by default at ~/.local/share/projector/venv, installs the CLI into it with pip, and links venv/bin/project into ~/.local/bin.

A venv doesn't carry its own Python. Its bin/python is a link to the interpreter that made it, and its pyvenv.cfg file records where that interpreter lives. When a version manager or an OS upgrade removes that interpreter, bin/python points at nothing. Before this change, the installer then ran python3 -m venv over the old directory, which failed with a bare No such file or directory, so neither a reinstall nor project upgrade could recover (issue #412).

This pull request makes the installer recognize that state and make the venv again with venv --clear, after the same Python 3.11 check it runs for a new venv. It also fixes a daemon test that failed whenever a checkout install left build metadata in src/ (issue #413).

groups.title: Rebuild a venv whose Python is gone
groups.kicker: The installer's no-pipx path remakes a broken venv instead of failing
intro: install_venv already skipped making a venv when bin/python was executable. That test is false for a link whose target is gone, so a broken venv reached the branch that makes a new venv. The change splits that branch: when pyvenv.cfg shows the directory is already a venv, it passes --clear, which empties the directory before Python's venv module builds it again, and prints a rebuilt row.

The venv holds only this install, so clearing it loses nothing that the following pip install doesn't put back. require_python still runs first, so a machine without Python 3.11 exits 69 with the venv as it was.

checks.text: Reproduced in a temporary HOME with a real Python 3.12 venv whose interpreter link was then deleted: main's installer exits 1 with [Errno 2] No such file or directory, and this head prints rebuilt, exits 0, and leaves a working project.

files.note: The new branch in install_venv that clears and remakes an existing venv.

checks.text: require_python runs before --clear: with PROJECTOR_PYTHON set to Python 3.9, or with no python3 on PATH, the installer exits 69 and a file left in the broken venv survives.
venv --clear unlinks symlinks instead of following them: files outside the venv, linked from its top level and from lib/, were intact after a rebuild.
A healthy venv is left alone: no venv command runs and pyvenv.cfg keeps its inode and modification time.

files.note: The fake python3 learns --clear, and a new test builds a venv with a dangling bin/python and checks the rebuild.

checks.text: test_without_pipx_a_venv_whose_python_is_gone_is_made_again fails against main's install.sh and passes at this head.

files.note: Says when PROJECTOR_PYTHON matters without pipx, and when the installer prints rebuilt.

groups.title: Keep a daemon test independent of build metadata
groups.kicker: A test asks the daemon as the version it recorded, not a fixed one
intro: Installing from a checkout leaves src/projector_cli.egg-info/, which is gitignored. With it on PYTHONPATH, the watch daemon a test starts records the real version, such as 0.8.12, instead of unknown. ensure_daemon replaces a running daemon whose version is older than the caller's, and the test asked as 1.0, so it got replaced where it expected running.
The test now asks as whatever version the daemon recorded, so it stays a test of starting and restarting a killed daemon.

checks.text: With an egg-info in src/, main's version of this test fails with ('replaced', 'started') and this head's passes.
